scope: Version-specific VCF semantics for unspecified alleles and reference-only blocks, including VCFv4.5 table VCF5.44.

semantics: Reference-only blocks may be represented in one record using INFO END.
Reference evidence is likelihood against unknown alternate allele <*>.
Worked examples use INFO END; no FORMAT LEN field appears in the section.
Retains the VCFv4.3 INFO END reference-block model and preference for <*> over <NON_REF>.
Worked examples use INFO END and no FORMAT LEN.
Uses <*> plus FORMAT LEN for reference-only blocks.
At positions implicitly called by a preceding <*> for a sample, GT must be missing and no FORMAT fields other than LAA may be present.
If LAA is present at a reference-block start for a sample, <*> must be included in that sample's LAA even when GT=0/0.
<NON_REF> should be treated as an alias of <*> for backward compatibility.
A missing FORMAT LEN should be inferred from INFO END if present.
Base-modification FORMAT values on a reference-block record apply to all applicable bases covered by the block.

changes: Introduces dedicated section for reference-only blocks using INFO END and <*>; prefers <*> over <NON_REF>.
FORMAT LEN is introduced to support sample-specific <*> reference-block lengths.
Per-sample implicit-call restrictions are added for GT and other FORMAT fields, with LAA exception.
LAA must include <*> at a reference-block start when present, even if GT=0/0.
<NON_REF> becomes a backward-compatible alias of <*> rather than merely a non-preferred alternative.
Missing FORMAT LEN is inferred from INFO END when present.
Base-modification values in a reference-block record apply to all applicable bases in the block.

example.interpretation: The table is informative; normative rules are the preceding prose. The records demonstrate both FORMAT LEN and redundant INFO END, including records with mixed variant/reference alleles.

scope_controls: Keep the gVCF project/producer conventions separate from the core VCF normative statements.
Do not infer that a producer's historical gVCF behavior is mandatory for every VCF producer.
Preserve the exact SHOULD force for the <NON_REF> alias and the exact MUST force for GT/LAA restrictions.

Do not assume FORMAT LEN can be reconstructed for every sample solely from a shared INFO END; the specification's sample-specific design exists because INFO END cannot represent different block lengths per sample.
remaining: Independent reviewer must verify the exact modal force and LAA/GT exception interactions.
Map the gVCF rules to atomic requirement IDs and per-version applicability.
Add positive/negative tests for mixed sample block lengths, absent/present LEN, END inference, NON_REF alias, GT missing restriction, extra FORMAT rejection and LAA inclusion.
No implementation or test execution is claimed.
